newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares seen steady, recovering from SAP.
newsitem.headline: German shares seen steady, recovering from SAP.

text.p: The German DAX index of 30 leading shares was expected to hold steady at new, lower levels on Wednesday and gradually recover from the blow dealt when SAP AG dived on a profit warning, sending the index tumbling.
But traders said the market would keep a keen eye on the U.S. and could post further losses if Wall Street closed much weaker. Early Dow weakness was already weighing, they said.
The IBIS DAX, which reflects computer trade in the DAX index, was down 1.49 percent, or 40.48 points at 2,681.26. The DAX had earlier closed floor trade down 19.45 points at 2,699.53.

Dealers said they did not expect the negative influence of SAP on the DAX to last too long. They said the news of the software firm's reduced profit forecast had hit an otherwise consolidating market and had taken away most of the downward correction potential in one go.

"I'd expect us to be more positive tomorrow," said one dealer, "Now that SAP has stabilised at these low levels and everybody who wanted to sell has done so, there could be a rebound in SAP shares tomorrow."
"I don't expect any more more large setbacks and I don't think there will be any more downward swings," he said.
Dealers said there would be some interest in the banking sector ahead of the nine-month reports of certain banks.
Deutsche Bank is due to publish nine-month results on Thursday, followed by Bayerische Vereinsbank on Friday.

Car maker Volkswagen AG climbed against the market trend, and was up 1.75 marks at 583 marks in IBIS dealings after the firm said its pre-tax profit soared during the first nine months of the year on what has been strong sales growth.
